tool_calls.name: inspect_image

params.question: What land cover and structures are visible? Look for industrial features, roads, mine infrastructure.
params.title: Sentinel-2 true colour, Yangquan City, Shanxi, 2025-09-08

tool_calls.saw:
The true-colour image shows a dense urban and industrial landscape: large warehouse-scale buildings with blue and red roofs, road networks, terraced hillsides, and multiple compound-style industrial facilities interspersed with residential blocks, consistent with a coal-mining city environment.

Ground record summary:
- **Heat:** VIIRS saw no heat source within 1 km over the last 30 nights; flaring was not observed.
- **Overture Maps:** 1 pipeline at the site, 2 industrial areas 1.8 km away; nothing mapped for mining, waste or wetland.
- **Registry:** The public registry (OGIM v3.0) lists no oil and gas facility within 2 km; a registry gap is not evidence of an empty site.
- **Coal mines:** The nearest coal mine on Global Energy Monitor's record is Yangquan No. 1 Coal Mine (operating), 4.2 km away; owners of record Yangquan Coal Industry Group (100%); parent of record Huayang New Material Technology Group; 6 other mines on its record within 10 km.

Now drafting the brief.

params.title: Sentinel-2 true colour, Yangquan City, Shanxi, 2025-09-08
params.description: Urban and industrial landscape with large compound-style facilities and terraced hillsides

observations: TROPOMI recorded a 14-day median anomaly of +124.7 ppb above background at this site (2026-10-06 to 2026-10-20), the highest of all nine watch areas scanned.

EMIT read 8 passes since 2025-01-01 and found 4 candidate passes (2025-08-18, 2025-09-25, 2025-09-29, 2025-11-30); peak enhancement on the strongest candidate was 5121.5 ppm·m with 1224 pixels at or above 1000 ppm·m.
The candidate window shows diffuse, scattered enhancement across the 6 km window with no single tight plume shape.
EMIT looked 28 times at this site (2024-01-30 to 2026-08-17); NASA outlined no plumes here in the plume product.
Carbon Mapper lists no plume within 5 km since 2025-01-01 (publication lag approximately 30 days).

explanations.next_check: Repeated candidate passes on new dates with consistent spatial pattern would support routine venting.
A single high-enhancement pass not repeated on adjacent dates would support an equipment failure.
A candidate pass coinciding with a known maintenance window would support a blowdown.
A flare stack mapped within 1 km with no VIIRS heat on the same night would support an unlit flare.
Aircraft or ground survey confirming coal mine ventilation shafts within the enhancement footprint would support a coal source.

gaps: NASA's plume product covers through 2025-09-22; passes after that date have not been checked for outlined plumes.
EMIT only sees this site on its passes; gaps between passes leave the record incomplete.
OGIM v3.0 lists no oil and gas facility within 2 km; absence from the registry is not evidence of an empty site.
Carbon Mapper's 30-day publication lag means detections from the past month may not yet appear.
params.next_collection: A new EMIT pass over this site with clear sky would confirm whether enhancement persists into late 2026.
